# Generated benchmark snapshot
# Command (post perf-review wave, 2026-08-09, working tree after lint wave + perf wave):
#   go test ./internal/convert -run '^$' -bench 'Benchmark(PDFPages|TemplatePages|WebFetchImage|ImageAssets)$' -benchmem -benchtime=1x -count=1
# Locked 500 PDF bar: 2.10s / 1.48GB / 3.93M allocs
# Separate locked-gate command: go test -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkPDFPages/500Pages$' -benchmem -benchtime=1x -count=3
# 500 PDF count-3 median after perf wave: 0.878s / 335.7MB / 517.9K allocs
# Toolchain: go1.26.4 linux/amd64 · Host: WSL2 24 CPUs · i7-13700HX
# Previous snapshot (pre perf wave, same day): PDF 500 = 1.013s / 392.2MB / 535K allocs.
# 500 PDF versus that snapshot: -14.4% B/op / -3.2% allocs (wall time is noisy one-shot).
# Main wave drivers: single cmap lookup per rune (GlyphAdvancePoints), no
# duplicate min-content re-measure, in-place inline-item compaction, ASCII
# fast paths in TextShow/html scanning, rune-union dedup in font subsetting,
# pointer-compare op sorts, zero-crossing split fast path, styleGroups hoist.
# Earlier wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 process reference: 2.05s / ~114MB peak RSS / ~2.0MB PDF.
# The wkhtmltopdf reference is process-level; Go B/op is cumulative allocation
# traffic, so it must not be presented as a direct RSS comparison.
